title: Buying US Stocks via GIFT City: Capital Gains & Dividend Tax Explained
description: Investing in US stocks through an IFSC unit in GIFT City offers a structured route for Indian residents and NRIs. Capital gains from transferring specified se.

faq.a: GIFT City is India's first operational International Financial Services Centre (IFSC) located in Gujarat, designed as a global financial and IT services hub with a competitive tax and regulatory environment.

Section 47(viiab) of the Income Tax Act exempts capital gains from the transfer of specified securities by an IFSC unit if the consideration is paid in foreign currency, making such gains tax-free in India.

faq.q: Will I pay tax in the US on my dividends?
faq.a: Yes, the US typically withholds tax on dividends paid to non-resident investors. Under the India-US DTAA, this rate is usually reduced from 30% to 15%.

faq.q: Can I claim a credit for US taxes paid?
faq.a: Yes, resident Indians can claim a Foreign Tax Credit (FTC) for the tax withheld in the US against their Indian income tax liability on the same dividend income, as per the DTAA and Indian tax laws.

faq.q: Is this route only for high-net-worth individuals?
faq.a: While GIFT City offers sophisticated investment avenues, it is becoming increasingly accessible to retail investors through various platforms. However, understanding the tax complexities is crucial, regardless of investment size.
Specified securities typically include shares, debentures, units of mutual funds, and other instruments as notified by the government, traded on a recognised stock exchange in the IFSC.

faq.q: Do NRIs investing via GIFT City pay tax in India?
faq.a: For NRIs, the tax implications depend on their tax residency status and the DTAA between India and their country of residence. Generally, if they are not tax residents of India, income not accruing or arising in India might not be taxable in India.
